dossier.valuation_method: Probability-of-success-weighted, time-discounted rNPV treating the common as a limited-liability call option on AP-SA02 approval, struck above ~$110M senior secured Innoviva debt and diluted across ~72M fully-diluted shares; scenario enterprise values anchored to antibiotic EV/peak-sales deal comps (~0.4-1.3x); discounted at a 13.8% cost of equity (10.8% CAPM + 3.0% size/illiquidity).
dossier.thesis_summary: Armata is the most advanced systemic-phage biotech, with a genuinely positive, adjudicated Phase 2a for AP-SA02 in S. aureus bacteremia and QIDP + Fast Track in hand. But the common is an out-of-the-money option: ~$4.75M cash with an unfunded ~$50-100M Phase 3 and going-concern doubt, sitting behind ~$110M of senior secured Innoviva term debt (14%, compounding) and diluted across ~72M fully-diluted shares (the reported ~36.6M is misleading), while Innoviva captures ~77-83% of any equity value. A ~22% PoS-to-approval (derived from anti-infective base rates) against antibiotic EV/peak comps of ~0.5-1.3x yields FMV ~$0.39/share, with ~78% of the distribution near zero.
key_value_drivers: AP-SA02 Phase 3 funding (pharma partnership / government pull funding vs dilutive raise) — the decisive catalyst
AP-SA02 PoS-to-approval ~22% (derived: 25% base x 0.7 SAB-superiority x 1.5 diSArm data-quality x 0.85 financing)
Commercial peak in a broken antibiotic market ($130-350M; EV/peak ~0.5-1.3x per Entasis/Achaogen comps; PASTEUR optionality)
Senior secured Innoviva debt ~$110M (14%, compounding) ahead of common; ~78% of outcome distribution leaves common near zero
Dilution: ~72M FD shares (convertible 19.7M @ $1.52 + 10.65M warrants + ~5M options); Innoviva control ~77-83%
key_risks: Financing failure / deeply dilutive raise transferring value from minority common
SAB superiority failure (exebacase/DISRUPT precedent: control arm regresses upward)
Senior-debt seniority and Innoviva control (acceleration via MAE/budget-deviation defaults; low-premium take-private)
Structurally broken hospital-antibacterial commercial market (Achaogen/Tetraphase/Melinta precedents)
Neutralizing antibodies / phage resistance limiting durability and re-dosing
what_would_change_my_mind: Non-dilutive Phase 3 funding (large pharma partnership upfront or BARDA/government pull funding)
PASTEUR Act or equivalent antibiotic subscription model enacted
Debt-for-equity restructuring removing the senior secured claim ahead of common
Phase 3 superiority replicating the diSArm relapse-prevention signal
Evidence of safe, effective repeat IV dosing addressing neutralizing-antibody risk

gaps: The base-case approval bridge ('~15% royalty on $250M + milestones ≈ $200M to Armata') is an approximation rather than a fully modeled royalty-NPV schedule; it is disclosed and sensitized, but an explicit year-by-year royalty NPV would tighten the single largest approval-path contributor.
The conditional commercial split (≈23%/54%/23% strong/base/weak) is reasonable but asserted rather than derived from an explicit distribution.
Section 4 summarizes management commentary well but does not quote the earnings call directly; a verbatim management quote on the Phase 3 financing plan would add color.
